# Adam Dittrich, PhD

<p class="inner-lede">Assistant Professor in the Department of Economic History at Prague University of Economics and Business. I work on monetary and financial history, interwar Central Europe, cliometrics, and the history of economic thought.</p>

<section class="cv-section">
<h2>Research and data</h2>
<div class="cv-entry"><div class="cv-date">National accounts</div><div>Czechoslovak contribution to a comparative Central and Eastern European GDP-reconstruction project with Matthias Morys and Marcin Wroński, focusing on agricultural output and value added, prices, intermediate inputs, and cross-country comparability.</div></div>
<div class="cv-entry"><div class="cv-date">Monetary history</div><div>Reconstruction of monthly Czechoslovak monetary and macroeconomic series from National Bank reports, 1926–1938, alongside comparative European sources.</div></div>
<div class="cv-entry"><div class="cv-date">Open research</div><div>Public replication projects on Czechoslovak financial stress, European bilateral trade, and Nordic trade resilience. <a href="data.qmd">Data and replication packages.</a></div></div>
<div class="cv-entry"><div class="cv-date">Manuscripts</div><div>Current research on monetary defence, trade adjustment, labour markets, historical national accounts, and Czech economic thought. <a href="publications.qmd">Publications and current papers.</a></div></div>
</section>

<section class="cv-section">
<h2>Methods and training</h2>
<p>Historical source criticism; archival, parliamentary and press research; central-bank balance-sheet reconstruction; index construction and decomposition; time-series and panel econometrics; PPML and gravity models; event studies; synthetic control and comparative counterfactual analysis.</p>
<div class="cv-entry"><div class="cv-date">2025</div><div><strong>International Monetary Fund training:</strong> Monetary Policy Analysis and Forecasting.</div></div>
<div class="cv-entry"><div class="cv-date">2023</div><div><strong>International Monetary Fund training:</strong> Macroeconomic Forecasting.</div></div>
</section>
